method.comparison: blind randomized A/B; side mapping read only after visual call

score.scale: 0-100 visual match to the official reference set

shots.note: Official frame has continuous rolling hills, dense layered vegetation, natural road edge and grounded contact; ours has card foliage and broad flat shoulder planes.
Official golden-hour exposure has coherent warm shadows and material texture; ours is washed around the sun with hard verge polygons and sparse repeated clumps.
Official night scene has readable headlight spill, road reflectance and layered dark silhouettes; ours is flatter and loses terrain/material detail in the shadows.
Official cockpit has believable road/shoulder and restrained dashboard framing; ours has an oversized dark dash and low-poly terrain ahead.
Official low-contrast view keeps natural hillside detail; ours is dominated by the cockpit shell and stamped autumn foliage on flat terrain.
Official elevated frame provides coherent lake, slope, road and tree depth; ours reads as a flat procedural field with visible polygon/card transitions.
Using terrestrial sr_13, official snow scene has soft valley layering and natural snow/road contact; ours achieves the palette but retains flat snow planes and billboard-like bare trees.

largest_gap: Continuous grounded landscape integration: replace hard-edged verge/snow polygons and repeated card-like foliage with blended near/mid/far terrain materials, contact shading, and coherent atmospheric depth. This gap persists across summer, golden, night, cockpit, vista, and winter views.
secondary_gaps: Cockpit camera framing and dashboard proportions are too dominant compared with the reference driving view.
Golden-hour and night lighting need stronger material response, shadows, and headlight/road interaction.
Winter palette is present, but snow coverage and distant valley layering remain procedural rather than continuous.
